Hi Sara —

Thanks for the clear list and the worksheet — very helpful. High-level answers we can include in the RFP packet (I'll paste below and attach the concise ratecard PDF):

- Streaming: we accumulate tokens per request and bill at request completion (we do not round per-chunk). For streaming tool responses, inbound partial chunks are buffered; final billing is based on the canonical tokenization of the complete messages as assembled by the runtime.
- System / assistant-initial messages: charged as input tokens. We separate line items in the invoice so tool/system tokens are visible but they are billed under the same input rate by default.
- Tool outputs: by default treated as output tokens from the service that generated them; if that output is then re-submitted as model input in a subsequent request, that re-submission is billed as input tokens as well (i.e., you can incur both sides).

I'll work with Ben and Karthik to provide a short formal paragraph and a sample calculation for the RFP (including rounding examples). Attaching redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf and a short technical note (redwood_rounding_memo.txt).

Adding the runtime / engineering perspective for the packet and the spreadsheet examples Sara sent:

- Token aggregation: billing uses the canonical tokenization of messages after the runtime reassembles streaming chunks. Practically: we compute the byte-level tokenization once the response completes; we do not increment billing per partial chunk, so micro-chunk rounding errors don't add up to extra cost for the customer.
- System prompts: these are included in the request's input token tally. For streaming chat where the assistant has an initial system message that is implicitly included by the API (not resubmitted each time), we amortize that system prompt across requests only when the customer configures session-level persistent context. In normal stateless requests each request's system text is counted.
- Toolcall case: there are two scenarios: (A) Synchronous toolcall where the tool executes and the tool output is returned within the same RPC -> that output is treated as assistant output tokens. (B) Tool output ingested in a subsequent request (for example, you store search results and later include them as input) -> then those tokens are charged as input in that later request. So you can definitely see charges on both sides depending on your integration.

- Rounding rule specifics (from memo): we round token counts to the nearest integer per-request after canonical tokenization. No per-chunk ceiling. For bulk invoices we sum request-level integers. This approach avoids tiny fractional charges and makes monthly reconciliations deterministic.

I'll add a short worked example for the spreadsheet where a 3.6-token average across chunks becomes 4 tokens at the request level (not per-chunk).

Hi Sara — following up with the formal language you can drop into your RFP and a proposed 12-month commitment discount schedule. Please feel free to copy verbatim.

RFP language (suggested):
Redwood Inference billing model (excerpt) — baseline hosted API
- Input tokens: all tokens submitted as user/system/instrumentation text to the model are billed at the published input rate. System messages injected by the platform or customer are included in the input token tally.
- Output tokens: tokens produced by the model in its generated response are billed at the published output rate.
- Tooling and integrations: text generated by outboard tools invoked by the model and returned inline to the user are initially billed as model output. If that tool-generated text is later re-submitted to the model as part of a separate request, those tokens are billed as input on that subsequent request.
- Rounding: token counts are computed using our canonical tokenization post-assembly of streaming data and rounded to the nearest integer per request. Monthly invoices sum per-request integers.

Proposed 12-month commitment pricing (hosted API) — Acme example tiers (US region):
- $0 - $1M annual spend: standard published rates (see attached redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf)
- $1M - $5M: 10% off published input/output rates
- $5M - $15M: 18% off published rates + dedicated billing cadence and single point of contact
- > $15M: bespoke pricing, committed SLAs, and potential dedicated capacity credits

Note: discounts apply to both input and output unit rates. Credits for burst capacity and waived onboarding credits can be negotiated separately.
